classification.difficultyReason: Choose the investment at 10% as the unknown, express the other portion as the remaining principal, and combine their percentage interests into an equation to expand and solve.

content.prompt: Trevor invests $\$10\,000$ for a year. He obtains $8\%$ per annum for a part of the money and $10\%$ per annum for the remainder. At the end of the year, he will receive $\$950$ in interest. How much does he invest at $10\%$?

answer.short:
$\$7500$

Express each portion’s one-year interest as a percentage of its principal and equate their sum to $\$950$.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ dollars be the amount invested at $10\%$. The amount invested at $8\%$ is $(10\,000-x)$ dollars.

$$\begin{align*}0.10x+0.08(10\,000-x)&=950\\0.10x+800-0.08x&=950\\0.02x+800&=950\\0.02x&=150\\x&=7500\end{align*}$$

Trevor invests $\$7500$ at $10\%$.
